title: Conditions for Redeeming Travel Credit against an Air Ticket Fare Brands Itinerary
content:
These are the conditions on which value standing on a traveller's travel credit vouchers may be put towards a new Air Ticket Fare Brands itinerary.

## 1. Conditions in force

1.1 **Order of consumption.** Vouchers are consumed in order of expiry, the soonest to lapse first, and where two vouchers lapse on the same date the one issued earlier is consumed first.

1.2 **The validity condition.** A travel credit is applied to a new itinerary only when frozen time is not after the moment the voucher was issued against the traveller's cancelled booking plus the credit validity term of the fare brand that produced it.

1.3 **How the term is counted.** Credit validity is counted in whole calendar months from the voucher issue date, and where the issue day does not exist in the expiry month the voucher lapses on the last day of that month.

1.4 **Who may redeem.** A voucher may only be redeemed by the traveller it was issued to, unless the fare brand that produced it makes credits transferable.

## 2. The validity condition in detail

| Element | What governs it |
| --- | --- |
| Clock | frozen time |
| Event the clock starts from | the moment the voucher was issued against the traveller's cancelled booking |
| Record that proves it | the voucher issue entry standing on that booking, with its voucher code and its stated expiry |
| Term added to it | the credit validity term of the fare brand that produced the voucher |
| Unit | whole calendar months |
| Direction of comparison | frozen time must be not after the anchor plus the term |
| Equality at the boundary | satisfies the condition |

The authority is the record, not the account given in the conversation: the voucher code and the issue entry on the booking decide the anchor, and the voucher the traveller quotes is the voucher whose entry is read.

## 3. Boundary cases, on hypothetical dates

A voucher produced by a brand whose credit validity term is 12 months and issued on 31 January lapses on 31 January of the following year; frozen time standing exactly on that day still satisfies the condition, because equality at the boundary satisfies it, while the following day does not.

A voucher issued on 31 March under a term of 12 months lapses on 31 March; a voucher issued on 31 August under a term counted to a month with no 31st lapses on the last day of that month, since the issue day does not exist there.

## 4. Clauses no longer in force

> "Travel credits issued from a traveller's cancelled bookings form one pool in that traveller's name, and a new itinerary may be paid for out of several vouchers at once."

That clause is **no longer in force**. The handling basis it stated has been superseded by the basis now governing the release of travel credit on Air Ticket Fare Brands bookings. The brand values scheduled under this policy are unaffected and stand as stated.

> "Where the pooled value exceeds the price of the new itinerary the remainder stays on the last voucher touched and keeps that voucher's original expiry; the expiry is never extended by redemption."

That clause is **no longer in force**. The handling basis it stated has been superseded by the basis now governing the release of travel credit on Air Ticket Fare Brands bookings. The brand values scheduled under this policy are unaffected and stand as stated.

> "Where the pooled value falls short the difference is collected in the original form of payment, and a partly paid itinerary is never ticketed."

That clause is **no longer in force**. The handling basis it stated has been superseded by the basis now governing the release of travel credit on Air Ticket Fare Brands bookings. The brand values scheduled under this policy are unaffected and stand as stated.

The conditions in section 1 are unaffected by those three retirements and remain in force as stated.
